## Current rendering and UI

The game is a browser-based detective story with a noir case-file presentation and an emerging comic-book style.

- **World view:** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`, especially `draw()`, `drawFirstPerson()` and `project()` (lines 56–65). The main canvas renders a perspective view of the town: gradient sky and ground, projected blocky buildings, lamps, a target marker and rain.
- **Town map:** The same file’s `drawTacticalMap()`, `toggleMap()`, `drawTownMap()` and `chooseMapRoute()` (lines 66–118). The map already has irregular districts, ink-edged roads, landmark plates, a route overlay, compass and atlas-style framing.
- **Other scene drawing:** `drawTown()`, `building()`, `tree()` and `drawPlace()` (lines 120–142) define a flatter overhead town scene. `drawTown()` does not appear to be called by the main render loop, so the active views to focus on are the first-person scene and tactical map.
- **UI structure:** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html` (lines 15–63) lays out a top bar, central scene with HUD and mobile controls, player/vitals bar, investigation sidebar, mobile navigation, and modal/toast roots.
- **Existing theme:** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/comic-theme.css` is loaded after the base `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css` in `index.html` (lines 11–12), so its overrides take precedence.

## Cohesive redesign opportunities

1. **Make the world canvas feel hand-inked—not just more saturated.**  
   The current scene uses simple rectangular facades and window shapes in `drawFirstPerson()` (game.js lines 61–64). The theme currently applies `saturate(1.65) contrast(1.22)` to `#world` and a halftone-like dot overlay to `.scene-wrap` (`comic-theme.css` lines 19–21). Build on that foundation with stronger dark outlines, selective shadow shapes, angular light and shadow, and restrained hatching in the canvas drawing itself. This will give the geometry a graphic-novel treatment instead of relying on a global filter alone.

2. **Make the map and world feel like parts of the same illustrated world.**  
   `drawTownMap()` already uses bold ink-backed roads, colored district shapes, landmark plates and orange/teal markers (game.js lines 69–118). Carry its visual language into the first-person view: use similarly dark outlines and consistent accent colors for the crime-scene cordon, destination marker and interactable buildings. Preserve the map’s clear atlas labels and route contrast so the comic treatment does not reduce readability.

3. **Push the interface toward printed case-file panels.**  
   The theme already establishes thick black borders and offset orange shadows for `.scene-wrap`, `.footbar` and `.case-sidebar`, plus bold treatment for lead cards, modals and buttons (comic-theme.css lines 18, 33, 40–61). To make that feel more unified, apply the same panel-edge and shadow logic consistently to smaller HUD and sidebar elements—especially `.scene-heading`, `.scene-coordinates`, `.pulse-card`, `.lead-card` and modal contents—without adding equally strong outlines to every element.

4. **Use a controlled palette with meaningful color roles.**  
   The theme defines comic black, paper, orange and teal (comic-theme.css lines 3–5). Keep orange for urgent leads, the active crime scene and primary actions; teal for navigation or confirmed information; and warm off-white for labels and paper-like surfaces. The existing distinction between `.lead-icon.crime`, `.lead-icon.witness` and `.lead-icon.symbol` (lines 45–49) is a useful starting point. Avoid turning every accent into a highlight, which would flatten the visual hierarchy.

5. **Treat evidence art as printed exhibits.**  
   The SVGs `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/images/mara-found.svg` and `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/images/scene-photograph.svg` already have borders, grain or rain, and embedded case-file captions. The theme styles `.scene-photo` and `.event-visual` as framed images (comic-theme.css lines 71–73). Keep the frame consistent with the broader panel system, and avoid piling another heavy texture over the artwork—the SVGs already contain their own texture and labels.

6. **Keep the HUD readable over a busier scene.**  
   The world canvas sits behind `.scene-vignette`, HUD labels, controls and `.rain-layer` (index.html lines 23–47). The theme adds a dot overlay and adjusts rain opacity (comic-theme.css lines 21–23, 75). If the world gets more textured, preserve clear backing behind the objective, coordinates, compass and interaction prompt. Check the mobile controls and navigation too; their overrides are already grouped under the theme’s mobile breakpoint (line 77 onward).

## Suggested priority

Start with the canvas rendering and the visual consistency between the first-person view and the already more developed tactical map. Then refine the UI panels and exhibit frames. The core interface already has a strong comic palette and outlined-panel treatment; the biggest opportunity is bringing the comparatively simple world rendering up to the same level.
